ROC analysis for gene signatures

rna_roc.Rd

Computes Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves and Area Under the Curve (AUC) for gene-level or multi-gene signatures using normalized RNA-seq data stored in the active rna_project.

This function provides a flexible framework to evaluate the discriminative performance of individual genes or gene sets in binary classification problems.

Usage

rna_roc(
  project,
  genes = NULL,
  group_col = "Group",
  score_method = c("auto", "pca", "mean"),
  show_gene_names = TRUE,
  line_color = "#1f77b4",
  plot = TRUE,
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

rna_project object created by rna_project().

genes

Character vector of gene symbols or Ensembl IDs, or "all" to use all genes.

group_col

Character. Column name in metadata defining binary groups.

score_method

Character. One of "auto", "pca", or "mean".

show_gene_names

Logical. Wheter to display gene names in subtitle.

line_color

Character. Optional plot line color (default: "#1f77b4").

plot

Logical. Whether to display the ROC curve.

save

Logical. Whether to store results in the active rna_project.

Value

An object of class "roc_result" containing:

roc_object

ROC object from pROC.

auc

Numeric AUC value.

auc_ci

Confidence interval for AUC.

genes

Genes used in the analysis.

method

Scoring strategy used ("single_gene", "logistic", or "signature").

score_method

Method used for multi-gene scoring ("pca" or "mean").

best_threshold

Optimal classification threshold (Youden index).

best_sens

Sensitivity at optimal threshold.

best_spec

Specificity at optimal threshold.

Details

The function adapts the prediction strategy based on the number of genes provided:

Single gene Expression values are directly used as predictor scores.

Small gene sets (<= 5 genes) A logistic regression model is fitted using gene expression as predictors.

Larger gene sets (> 5 genes) A composite signature score is computed:

  • pca: first principal component (default in "auto" mode)

  • mean: average expression across genes

The ROC curve is computed using pROC, and the optimal threshold is determined using the Youden index.

Gene identifiers can be provided as Ensembl IDs or gene symbols. When possible, gene symbols are retrieved automatically using biomaRt.

Interpretation guide

  • AUC ~ 0.5 indicates no discriminative ability

  • AUC 0.7–0.8 indicates moderate performance

  • AUC 0.8–0.9 indicates strong performance

  • AUC > 0.9 may indicate very strong signal or potential overfitting

For multi-gene signatures, interpretation depends on how the score is constructed. PCA-based scores capture dominant variance structure, while mean-based scores assume consistent directionality across genes.

Important considerations

Binary outcome required The grouping variable must contain exactly two levels.

Unsupervised signatures PCA-based scoring does not use class labels and may not yield optimal classification.

Large gene sets Using "all" genes may produce unstable or uninterpretable results, especially without prior feature selection.

Data leakage When evaluating predictive performance, avoid using genes selected from the same dataset without proper validation.

Pipeline context

This function is typically used after rna_normalize() and optionally after feature selection steps such as rna_compare(). It complements visualization tools like rna_heatmap() by providing quantitative classification metrics.

Side effects

If save = TRUE, results are stored in the rna_project under the analyses$roc slot.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Single gene ROC
rna_roc(project = my_project,
        genes = "CD8A"
)

# Multi-gene logistic model
rna_roc(my_project,
        genes = c("CD3D", "CD8A", "GZMB")
)

# Signature using PCA score
rna_roc(my_project,
        genes = c("Gene1", "Gene2", "Gene3", "Gene4", "Gene5", "Gene6"),
        score_method = "pca"
)
} # }
